programme.title: Michael Palin and the Mystery of Hammershoi
programme.desc: Michael Palin goes on a very different adventure, exploring the secretive life of Danish artist Vilhelm Hammershoi. Leaving few personal clues behind on his death, Michael works hard to reveal the man behind the mystery.

programme.title: Nobody's Perfect: The Making of Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: Revealing documentary about the creation and shooting of the acclaimed comedy movie. Including interviews with stars Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis and behind-the-scenes colour footage.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: How to Write a Mills and Boon
programme.desc: To mark 100 years of romance publishers Mills and Boon, literary novelist Stella Duffy takes on the challenge of writing for them. Romantic fiction is a global phenomenon, and Mills and Boon are among the biggest names in the business. The company welcomes submissions from new authors, but as Duffy soon finds out, writing a Mills and Boon is harder than it looks.

programme.title: Britain's Pompeii: A Village Lost in Time
programme.desc: Professor Alice Roberts joins the team excavating a 3,000-year-old Bronze Age village in the Cambridgeshire Fens that's been called the 'British Pompeii'. The village earned its nickname because, 3,000 years ago, it burned to the ground - as it burned, it fell into the peat, preserving both the houses and their contents. Until its discovery, we had little real idea of what life was like in Bronze Age Britain.

programme.title: Art of America
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon embarks on an epic journey from east to west, following in the footsteps of the pioneers who built the foundations of modern America. He travels to Massachusetts to see the earliest portraits in America depicting the Puritan settlers and visits Pennsylvania to uncover the dark truth behind Benjamin West's most famous painting, the `Treaty of Penn with the Indians'.

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes explains how America was shaped by Europeans, Spaniards in the south-west, Pilgrims in the north-east and struggling cavaliers in Virginia, who saw the New World as both paradise and hell.

programme.title: Leonora Carrington: The Lost Surrealist
programme.desc: British surrealist Leonora Carrington was a key part of the surrealist movement during its heyday in Paris and yet, until recently, remained a virtual unknown in the country of her birth. This film explores her dramatic evolution from British debutante to artist in exile, living out her days in Mexico City, and takes us on a journey into her darkly strange and cinematic world.

programme.title: This Is Joan Collins
programme.desc: Joan narrates her seven rollercoaster decades in showbiz. A worldwide television phenomenon with her decade-defining role in 'Dynasty', Collins shares her extraordinary home archive footage, giving an intimate glimpse into one of the world's most iconic figures.

programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: A look at the social and economic changes which took place during the reign of Queen Victoria. Industrialisation had a huge impact, and some believed that the machine age would bring about the destruction of the vital bonds that held communities together. Meanwhile, many women were leaving their traditional roles at the centre of the home and family to find new roles in reshaping society.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: Cassius Clay worked his way up from amateur boxer to Olympic gold medallist in 1960. Clay turned professional and moved to Miami, where he trained and taught himself how to promote. In 1962, he defeated Sonny Banks in his first fight.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.desc: After his first victory, Clay won every fight. He is introduced to the Nation of Islam and becomes a confidant of Malcolm X. In 1964, he beats Sonny Liston and becomes heavyweight champion.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.sub-title: Round Two: What's My Name? Part 1
programme.desc: Cassius Clay joins the Nation of Islam and adopts the name Muhammad Ali. For three years Ali dominated the heavyweight ranks, but in 1967 he refused service for the Vietnam War in the U.S. Army.

programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.sub-title: Round Two: What's My Name? Part 2
programme.desc: Muhammad Ali dominated the heavyweight ranks for three years. In 1967, he refused service for the Vietnam War and became one of the most reviled men in America. Ali is stripped of his title.

programme.title: Little Ships - The Miracle of Dunkirk
programme.desc: To mark the 70th anniversary of the 'miracle of Dunkirk', fifty of the surviving 'Little Ships' which made the original perilous cross-channel voyage, are returning to France. Dan Snow tells the extraordinary story of these Little Ships, their role in the evacuation and the people who struggled to keep them afloat during those fateful days in 1940, when the future of Europe hung in the balance.

programme.title: The Hadron Collider: In Search of the Peace Particle

programme.title: Too Near the Sun
programme.desc: Documentary, first broadcast in 1966, that tells the history of the superbomb, exploring the race by scientists to imitate the nuclear reactions of the sun and build the first thermonuclear weapon. The film reveals how the careers and reputations of some of the scientists involved were seared in the process.
